cards.d: To assess something means to judge the structure, purpose, or quality of it.
cards.e: She assessed the condition of the toy car before buying it.
cards.ielts: Teachers should assess students through projects and presentations, not only through written examinations.

cards.d: To astonish someone means to greatly surprise them.
cards.e: The amount of people that came to her party astonished her.
cards.ielts: The speed at which smartphones spread across developing countries has astonished many economists.

cards.d: To commence something means to begin it.
cards.e: His speech commenced with a “thank you” to all who had helped him succeed.
cards.ielts: Construction of the new metro line will commence next year and is expected to take five years to complete.

cards.d: The essence of something is its important qualities or basic characteristics.
cards.e: The essence of the argument was that both sides felt they had lost money.
cards.ielts: The essence of good education is teaching young people how to think, not simply what to remember.

cards.d: To extract something means to remove it.
cards.e: The dentist extracted the woman’s damaged tooth and put in a fake one.
cards.ielts: Mining companies extract huge quantities of minerals each year, often leaving behind polluted land and water.

cards.d: If something is fabulous, it is extremely good.
cards.e: This strawberry is the best I’ve ever had. It’s fabulous.
cards.ielts: If I could visit any city again, I would return to Samarkand, because the architecture there is absolutely fabulous.

cards.d: Haste is speed in movement or action.
cards.e: In order to get to the meeting in time, he proceeds with haste.
cards.ielts: Laws passed in haste after a crisis are often poorly designed and have to be changed later.

cards.d: An impulse is a sudden thoughtless urge to do something.
cards.e: Because of the scary noise, she had an impulse to run somewhere and hide.
cards.ielts: Online shops are designed to encourage customers to buy on impulse, which can lead some people into serious debt.

cards.d: Latter describes something last in a series or the second choice of two things.
cards.e: In the latter minutes of the game, the visitors scored the winning goal.
cards.ielts: Given the choice between living in the city and the countryside, I would choose the latter, because it is quieter and less polluted.

cards.d: A molecule is the smallest basic unit that makes up a physical substance.
cards.e: A tiny drop of water is made up of thousands of molecules of water.
cards.ielts: Scientists are developing filters that can capture carbon dioxide molecules directly from the atmosphere.

cards.d: If something is ongoing, then it is still happening or still growing.
cards.e: The development of plants is ongoing because it takes time for them to mature.
cards.ielts: The ongoing debate about university fees shows no sign of ending, as both sides present strong arguments.

cards.d: If something is pharmaceutical, then it is related to the development of drugs.
cards.e: Pharmaceutical companies discover new cures to illnesses all the time.
cards.ielts: Pharmaceutical companies argue that high drug prices are necessary to fund research into new treatments.

cards.d: If someone is precise, then they are exact and careful about their work.
cards.e: The builder was very precise about where he placed the nails.
cards.ielts: Doctors need precise data about patients' lifestyles in order to give useful advice on preventing heart disease.

cards.d: Proximity is closeness in time, space, or relationships.
cards.e: All the trees in the proximity of the beach had been cut down.
cards.ielts: House prices tend to be higher in close proximity to good schools and public transport.

cards.d: Publicity is public attention given to someone or something by the media.
cards.e: She received a lot of publicity after her performance in the film.
cards.ielts: The campaign against plastic straws received enormous publicity after a video of an injured turtle went viral.

cards.d: A remedy is a cure for a disease, argument, or problem.
cards.e: A good remedy for a headache is an aspirin and a glass of water.
cards.ielts: Planting more trees is often suggested as a simple remedy for air pollution in crowded cities.

cards.d: The significance of something is the quality that makes it important.
cards.e: The significance of the snowy weather was that we didn’t have to go to school.
cards.ielts: The significance of the internet for modern education can hardly be overstated, especially in remote areas.

cards.d: If something is subsequent, then it comes after something else in time.
cards.e: The flood and the subsequent rescue of those caught in the flood were on TV.
cards.ielts: The factory closed in 2010, and the subsequent rise in unemployment led many young people to leave the town.

cards.d: If something is synthetic, then it is made to be like something natural.
cards.e: Clothing made out of synthetic fabrics is very effective at keeping people warm.
cards.ielts: Synthetic fabrics release tiny plastic fibres when washed, which eventually end up in rivers and oceans.

cards.d: If something is terminal, then it causes or results in death.
cards.e: Since his condition was not terminal, he felt a great sense of relief.
cards.ielts: Whether patients with a terminal illness should have the right to end their lives remains a controversial ethical question.
